Yes, I was really impressed with that  performance today. I thought it was a  
really good team performance. It’s just  a continuation of the really good run  
that we’re on away from home—four  wins out of five—and I think we’ve  
earned every one of those victories.  It was another really good performance.
A lot was said about our away form, and  it was important to change that. But also,  
what was really important was that  after we got the first victory,  
we built on it and added to it. That’s  exactly what we’ve done, so I’m delighted.
Our focus now is on the remaining seven games  until the split. We’ve spoken as a group about  
how many points we can accumulate in that spell  and about just focusing on ourselves. We know how  
tight the league is, how many good teams there  are in it, and that a lot of teams around us  
are in good form. But we can’t get affected  by that. We just have to focus on ourselves,  
and that’s exactly what we did today.  We come off with three points, and now  
we move on to another important  game next week against Dundee.
Having a striker like Jordan White in form and up  to 12 goals now gives you a real chance in matches  
and puts you in control. Jordan is a penalty-box  striker—you have to create opportunities for him,  
and when he gets them, he’s very clinical.  I think he could have been better in terms  
of his overall performance within the  game, and he’ll be the first to admit  
that. But I’m sure he’ll be delighted at  the same time to come away with two goals.
It’s been a really good return for him,  especially considering the transition  
he’s made from part-time football to coming  to our club and having such a big impact this  
season. And of course, now there’s the Northern  Ireland opportunity for him as well. He’s had  
to be patient for that, but I’m sure that’ll  come along. He’s really keen for it to happen,  
but what’s important is that he concentrates  on playing well for Ross County and continuing  
his individual performances. If he does  that, I’m sure he’ll get a call-up soon.
As a football manager, you can’t take your  birthday off work, but getting a victory like that  
must give you a lot of satisfaction—even if your  birthday gets pushed to the back of your mind. We  
know the industry that we’re in, and it just  so happens that my birthday falls on today.  
I did ask the players last night, when I was  presented with a birthday cake at the hotel,  
if they could give me three points—and  they duly obliged. So, thank you to them.
You really can’t get a better present than  that. It was an important game, an important  
three points, and it just happens to be my  birthday as well. Now, it means I can have  
a nice journey back up the road on the  bus and then celebrate when I get home.
The long trips back home can feel much longer  if the result doesn’t go your way. But tonight,  
it’ll feel a lot better. It definitely does make  a difference. When things don’t go your way,  
you have a long time to sit and think  about the game and analyze it. But  
today, everything is positive. I  saw a lot of really good things,  
and the boys should be really proud  of the performance they put in.
It was quite a strike from the captain near the  end to cap things off. Yes, it was about time!  
He’s been in that position numerous times this  season. He’s been a little bit unfortunate at  
times, and at other times, I think he could  have done better. So, I’m delighted for him.  
He’s the captain of this football club, and  he’s everything you would want in a captain—the  
way he conducts himself every single day  at our club. It was nice for him to have  
that moment to celebrate, scoring a goal for  all the effort that he puts in for his team.
As for our traveling support, no matter  how small or big the away crowd is,  
it means everything to us as a group. Seeing them  there, celebrating with them—it’s special. It’s  
obviously even better when we win,  and they’re rowdy and bubbly. But I  
think over these last two months, especially away  from home, they’ve seen a team that is giving  
everything for their football club. I’m sure  they’ll be travelling back home happy tonight.
title: Don Cowie Post Match Press Conference | Motherwell 0-3 Ross County
